newsitem.title: UK: IPE makes major changes to natgas futures contract.
newsitem.headline: IPE makes major changes to natgas futures contract.

text.p: The International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) announced a series of changes to its recently-launched natural gas futures contract, approved at a meeting of the Gas Working Group on Tuesday afternoon.
Changes to the Energy Trading System (ETS), the electronic trading system used to trade the contract, will allow several changes on August 8.

These include the facility to trade the Balance of the Month contract on the ETS; longer trading hours from 1000 hrs to 1700 hrs with no break; the insertion of a decimal place at the keying-in stage on the ETS; and an increase in the minimum tick size from 0.005 pence to 0.01 pence a therm.
The IPE added in a statement that these changes are subject to its regular approval procedures.

The exchange has also announced the approval of a new regulatory regime for traders. This will allow trade associate members of the IPE to be regulated directly by the IPE itself as their front line regulator.

Trade associate members will not require authorisation by either the Securities and Futures Authority or the Securities and Investments Board. The IPE believes that easing the regulatory burden will encourage more participants to come into the market.
Trade associate members will trade directly using a gas trading right leased from a Floor Member of the Exchange. Floor members will continue to clear for trade associates.
Measures to improve trading anonymity are also being planned and will be in place by the end of August.
And the IPE is considering establishing a market maker scheme to ensure quotes are available in all months listed within as tight a bid/offer spread as possible.
